question: Why are so many of the world's best distance runners from a few highland areas of Kenya and Ethiopia?
answer: A mix of factors, Epstein argues: living and training at altitude, slender builds with thin lower legs that are cheaper to swing, a strong running culture, and for some, running long distances as children. No single gene explains it, and he warns against both genetic determinism and denying that biology plays a part.
move: Big differences usually have several causes; beware single explanations.
simply: Great Kenyan and Ethiopian runners come from high places, often have thin legs, run a lot as kids, and grow up surrounded by runners. It all adds up.
why: When a group excels at something, the honest answer usually combines geography, culture and biology. Single-cause stories are tempting and usually wrong.
reference: David Epstein, The Sports Gene: Inside the Science of Extraordinary Athletic Performance (Current, 2013), ch. 12
